2026-08-05 audit, same bug class as 'divórcio e desabafa' one tier up. The weak tier read search_secondary_tokens (a NearText attribute) and not search_secondary (the index field), so an exact hashtag/summary match the attribute cannot mirror had no rung and died at text_score_cutoff. Three routes: STEMMING (now CLOSED — every text field carries `stemming: none` as of 2026-08-05, for the larger language reason recorded under the 'esposa' case; it had been the reachable one, the plural reaching the index and not the prefix column), words under FuzzyWordGroup.MIN_PREFIX_LEN ('#ai'), and words past NearText.MAX_ELEMENTS in a long description. Fixed by secondary_match(); RankRegressionIT pins the two repo-determined routes ('ai', 'quilombola'), the stemmer-dependent one is comment-only. Run this against a corpus with a '#bitcoiner' hashtag and no 'bitcoiners' anywhere.

2026-08-05 audit, FIXED. nip05/lud16 were the last matchable columns with no rung. bm25 alone decided both WHETHER such a hit ranked and WHERE, and that conflation was the bug: a common-domain match diluted to ~0 was meant to rank last, but text_score() has a cutoff, so it was deleted. Worse, matchCount on either field flipped has_token_match, hence any_token_match, which gates weak_match and tier_body_match — so an identity match suppressed every rung beneath it, including affil_tokens, the weak column built for those very fields. FIX: any_token_match() is now name-or-title only (has_token_match retired), and identity is one of weak_match()'s signals — so band membership is categorical and identity_text()'s IDF dilution orders hits from WITHIN the weak band instead of deciding whether they rank at all. A unique handle sorts far above a mass-hosted domain; neither can reach the name band. No new weight: an UNFINISHED word touching these fields already landed in weak via the affil_tokens prefix, so a finished word landing in the same band needs no recalibration. Retires the affiliation_match/affiliation_match_text and secondary_active/secondary_active_text forks that the same asymmetry had forced, and makes tierOf's "identity" label reachable for the first time (it was dead from the day it was written: identity implied has_token_match, so "name" always claimed it). Verified against a live Vespa: RankRegressionIT green with the recall-floor matrix asserting nip05/lud16 -> identity, and SearchPrefixLadderIT — the suite whose corpus has docs reachable ONLY through lud16/nip05 — green.

2026-08-05, MEASURED and FIXED. Non-English body text was unsearchable: Vespa stems a DOCUMENT's index terms with the language it DETECTS, while a query carries no language and is stemmed as English, and nothing here set either side. On a Portuguese note the two never met except on a word with no suffix to strip — measured, same words, only the query language differing: default(en) futebol 1 / esposa 0 / crise 0 / desabafa 0 / divorcio 0; model.language=pt all 1. This is why the reported 'divórcio e desabafa' note needed more than the body rung. FIX: `stemming: none` on every text field (name/display_name/search_primary already had it), so both sides are raw and agree by construction in any language. Measured cost: none — English stemming was already inert here ('wolf' does not find 'wolves', 'run' does not find 'running'), identical before and after. Rejected alternative: forcing one document language, which also worked but pins TOKENIZATION and would foreclose segmenting CJK. STILL BROKEN and pinned separately: CJK body text, which is a segmentation (tokenization) problem needing a CJK-capable linguistics component. Upgrade: fresh deploys unaffected (verified); redeploying over an existing cluster needs a validation-overrides.xml allowing indexing-change plus a Vespa reindex — reindexFullTextSearch will NOT do it.

2026-08-05 audit, MEASURED and fixed. text_score_cutoff justifies itself with a gram-only ceiling of ~93 (gram_cap 80 + the about fallback), but only name_text() and tier_primary_text() capped their gram term — about_text() and secondary_text() did not, so the ceiling was asserted, not enforced. Measured on a live Vespa with docs whose search_secondary holds the query word ONLY as an infix inside a larger token (exact clause and *_tokens prefix both miss; real_match 0): bitcoin/w_gram 2.0 -> 18-20, bitcoin/8.0 -> 74-78, extraordinary/2.0 -> 37-43, extraordinary/8.0 -> 149-172 — the last CROSSING the cutoff and being returned as a hit. w_gram flips to 8.0 when the SHORTEST query word is <=3 chars and then applies to every word, so a two-word query like this one is the trigger: the long word supplies the trigram count, the short one the weight. Capping both terms puts the same rows at 32 (= w_secondary 0.4 x gram_cap 80) and the hit is dropped. about never crossed on its own (w_about 0.1 damps a measured about_text of 282 to 28) but was capped too, so the cutoff's arithmetic is true again. Rank-profile-only change: deploys with no validation override and no reindex. RankRegressionIT green with it.
